standard.title: Investigate drama to challenge meaning
standard.description: investigate use of elements of drama, performance skills and/or conventions to communicate and/or challenge ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in drama across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can investigate how elements and conventions communicate meaning in drama across cultures, times and places (Y7-8). They can analyse and evaluate use of elements and conventions in drama they experience or participate in.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how elements of drama, performance skills and conventions are used to communicate and/or challenge ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in drama across cultures, times, places and other contexts.

nodes.label: Drama that challenges — identifying the 'challenge' move
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify when and how drama is being used to challenge — not just communicate — ideas, perspectives or meaning, and describe the specific dramatic devices doing that work.
nodes.minimum_width: Student identifies at least one example of drama that challenges a dominant perspective or meaning, and names at least one dramatic device used to create the challenge.
nodes.typical_width: Students view examples of drama from diverse styles or forms — historical, modern, from Australia and Asia — to identify how conventions are used to communicate and challenge; they identify how contemporary performance styles (mediatisation, intertextuality, physical theatre) affect meaning; they consider actor-audience relationships in different dramatic contexts.
wider: Students investigate how drama that uses satire, irony or Brechtian distancing to challenge ideas operates differently from drama that seeks to create identification and empathy
Students investigate drama from a country or region in Asia considering the social, cultural and historical context in which it challenges or affirms dominant meanings
nodes.hinge_reason: The 'challenge' dimension — drama as a site of contestation, not just communication — is new at Y9-10; without students grasping how dramatic form can be used to disrupt rather than confirm, their analysis stays at the level of communication and misses the critical dimension of the descriptor.

response_modes.reason: Use comparative analysis: show two dramas treating the same theme, one that communicates a perspective and one that challenges it; make the distinction explicit before asking students to analyse independently.

success_criteria: Student identifies at least one drama that challenges a perspective or meaning
Student names at least one specific dramatic device used to create that challenge and explains how it works

nodes.label: Investigating conventions, context and cultural challenge across drama
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how performance conventions, context and cultural position shape whether and how drama communicates or challenges — across diverse cultural, historical and contemporary examples.
nodes.minimum_width: Student investigates at least two drama examples from different cultural, historical or contextual positions and analyses how each uses conventions to communicate or challenge.
nodes.typical_width: Students view examples of varied styles/forms to understand how conventions are shared and differ across styles; they consider questions of social context, cultural movement, historical influence and actor-audience relationships; they use Viewpoints-style analysis to frame their investigation.
wider: Students investigate how First Nations Australian drama that challenges colonial narratives operates — identifying the specific conventions and structural choices that make the challenge culturally and dramatically effective

Students investigate a contemporary global drama phenomenon (mediatisation, site-specific performance, immersive theatre) and analyse how it reframes the audience relationship and challenges traditional dramatic conventions

response_modes.reason: The depth of understanding available through wide exposure to diverse drama traditions — including contemporary, non-Western and challenging forms — is the substance of this standard.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Investigating drama that challenges meaning across diverse cultural traditions, historical periods and contemporary forms is very rich; students who investigate widely develop substantially stronger critical and analytical capacity.
success_criteria: Student analyses at least two drama examples from different contexts, explaining how each uses conventions to communicate or challenge
Student identifies how social, cultural or historical context shapes the drama's meaning or challenge
